How do you start a presentation? Many people start with: Sorry, I'm a little nervous. Please don't. Your audience decides in the first minute if they want to listen. Here is a simple plan for a strong opening. First of all, say hello and thank people for coming. Second, say who you are, in one sentence. Then tell the audience the purpose of your talk: why are they here? After that, give a short overview of your main points. Three main points are perfect. Ten points are too many. Finally, tell people when they can ask questions. Do all this in about one minute. Remember: a good opening is not long. It's clear.

Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for coming. My name is Daniel Visser, and I'm the head of logistics at Harbor Fresh Foods. The topic of today's presentation is how fruit travels from the farm to the supermarket. The purpose of this talk is to show you our rules for new suppliers. I have three main points. To begin with, I'll talk about temperature. Then I'll move on to packaging. Finally, I'll explain our delivery times. You can find all the details in the handout on your table. The talk is about twenty minutes, and there will be time for questions at the end. So, let's begin with temperature.
